elections.summary: Social Democrats (S) finished first with 99 of 349 seats on 28.0% of the vote. Turnout 84.9%.
Prosperity Party finished first with 438 of 547 seats. Turnout 95.7%.
elections.caveat: Voting did not take place in Tigray or in parts of Amhara and Oromia because of conflict, leaving 61 of 547 seats vacant.

elections.summary: Tisza Party finished first with 141 of 199 seats on 53.2% of the vote. Turnout 79.0%.

General elections were held in Denmark on 24 March 2026. All 179 seats in the Folketing were up for election, including 175 in Denmark proper, 2 in Greenland, and 2 in the Faroe Islands (the three entities making up the Danish Realm).
Communist Party of Vietnam finished first with 482 of 500 seats. Turnout 99.7%. Lê Minh Hưng replaced Phạm Minh Chính.
elections.caveat: Nearly 93% of the 864 candidates for 500 seats were Communist Party members and only 5 were self-nominated; an independent journalist was arrested and beaten by police after criticising the election's legitimacy online.

elections.summary: Bangladesh Nationalist Party finished first with 210 of 350 seats. Turnout 59.4%. Tarique Rahman took office.
Bhumjaithai Party finished first with 192 of 500 seats on 17.9% of the vote. Turnout 71.4%. Anutin Charnvirakul stayed in office.

The election took place nearly four months into Sanae Takaichi's tenure as Prime Minister of Japan, which began on 21 October after she won the 2025 Liberal Democratic Party presidential election and formed the Liberal Democratic Party–Japan Innovation Party coalition (LDP–JIP).

Early general elections were held in the Netherlands on 29 October 2025 to elect the members of the House of Representatives. The elections had been expected to be held in 2028, but a snap election was called after the Schoof cabinet collapsed due to the Party for Freedom (PVV) withdrawing from the coalition.
Labour Party finished first with 53 of 169 seats on 28.0% of the vote. Turnout 80.1%.
Jamaica Labour Party finished first with 35 of 63 seats on 50.5% of the vote. Turnout 40.0%. Andrew Holness stayed in office.
A conclave was held on 7 and 8 May 2025 to elect a new pope to succeed Francis, who had died on 21 April 2025. Of the 135 eligible cardinal electors, all but two attended.
General elections were held in Singapore on 3 May 2025 to elect members of Parliament.
elections.caveat: Cleanly counted but structurally tilted: GRC wards, government-aligned media and litigation against opposition figures shape the field long before polling day.

elections.summary: A federal election was held on 3 May 2025 to elect members of the 48th Parliament of Australia. All 150 seats in the House of Representatives were up for election, along with 40 of the 76 seats in the Senate.

Mark Carney, Prime Minister for barely six weeks, led the Liberals to a fourth consecutive term in an election dominated by Donald Trump's tariffs and talk of annexation. The Liberals and Conservatives together took over 85% of the vote, the highest two-party share since 1958; Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre lost his own Ottawa-area seat even as his party gained ground.

A federal election was held in Germany on 23 February 2025 to elect the 630 members of the 21st Bundestag, down from 736 in 2021 due to reforms in seat distribution. The 2025 election took place seven months ahead of schedule due to the 2024 collapse of the Scholz governing coalition.

Trump completed the only Cleveland-style comeback, winning the popular vote as well as all seven battlegrounds, the first Republican popular win since 2004. Harris, elevated late after Biden's withdrawal, was the shortest-notice major-party nominee of the modern era.

General elections were held in Japan on 27 October 2024 due to the early dissolution of the House of Representatives, the lower house of the National Diet, by Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba. Voting took place in all constituencies, including proportional blocks, to elect all 465 members of the House of Representatives.

Starmer's Labour won 411 seats on just 33.7% of the vote, the most disproportional result in British history, as Reform UK split the right and the Conservatives fell to 121 seats, their worst ever. Five parties took over a million votes each.

The first election of the post-Brexit Union returned a Parliament shifted rightward: the radical right now filled three groups, with Viktor Orbán's new Patriots for Europe becoming the third-largest, while the Greens and liberals gave back their 2019 gains. The EPP alone gained seats among the big groups, and Ursula von der Leyen was confirmed for a second Commission term.

After a lengthy government formation spanning 494 days, the 2019 Belgian federal election eventually resulted in the formation of a government led by prime minister Alexander De Croo, consisting of a so-called Vivaldi coalition.

General elections were held in India from 19 April to 1 June 2024 in seven phases, to elect all 543 members of the Lok Sabha. Votes were counted and the result was declared on 4 June to form the 18th Lok Sabha.

General elections were held in South Africa on 29 May 2024 to elect a new National Assembly as well as the provincial legislature in each of the nine provinces. This was the seventh general election held under the conditions of universal adult suffrage since the end of the apartheid era in 1994.
Pakistan Muslim League (N) finished first with 98 of 336 seats on 23.6% of the vote. Turnout 47.8%. Shehbaz Sharif took office.
elections.caveat: A Supreme Court ruling stripped Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf of its electoral symbol before the vote, so its candidates stood as independents, and the party's website and voter helpline were blocked in the country.

elections.summary: Presidential elections were held in Taiwan on 13 January 2024 as part of the 2024 general elections. Tsai Ing-wen of the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), the incumbent president of the Republic of China, was ineligible for reelection due to term limits.
Awami League finished first with 271 of 350 seats. Turnout 41.8%. Sheikh Hasina stayed in office.
elections.caveat: The BNP boycotted after a crackdown on its leaders; the US State Department said the vote was not free and fair, and the UK government said it lacked the preconditions of democracy.

elections.summary: Early general elections were held in the Netherlands on 22 November 2023 to elect the members of the House of Representatives. The elections had been expected to be held in 2025, but a snap election was called after the fourth Rutte cabinet collapsed on 7 July 2023 due to disagreements on immigration policy between the coalition parties.

Federal elections were held in Switzerland on 22 October 2023 to elect all members of the National Council and Council of States. The elections were followed by elections to the Federal Council, Switzerland's government and collegial presidency, on 13 December.
General elections were held in Argentina on 22 October 2023 to elect the president, vice president, members of the National Congress, and the governors of most provinces.
A general election took place in New Zealand on 14 October 2023 to determine the composition of the 54th New Zealand Parliament.
Independents finished first with 20 of 40 seats. Turnout 44.0%.
elections.caveat: The 20 elected seats are chosen not by citizens at large but by an electoral college the rulers of each emirate select, and the other 20 seats in the council are simply appointed by those same rulers.
